parsed.explanation: Combined federal-state regime imposes universal traveller-facing exposures: birth-sex passport/facility rules, discrepancy-based entry refusal and possible fraud inadmissibility, state bathroom restriction and a documented trespass arrest with 24 hours in a men's ward, plus immigration-custody reports of forced labour, beatings and sexual abuse. State compounds this with bans on birth-certificate changes, no state gender-identity anti-discrimination or hate-crime cover, and minor care, sports, pronoun and parental-disclosure restrictions. Courts, litigation, injunctions on some orders, national hate-crime/employment protections and broad anti-discrimination support mitigate, but core passport and facility policies remain operative and efficiently enforced, so recourse does not cancel exposure. No execution or routine imprisonment is documented.

entry_documents.exposure: Binary birth-sex passport policy; X/new mismatched passports not processed, existing X valid to expiry. 2025 cable: document discrepancy leads to refusal and added evidence; suspected wilful misrepresentation may support permanent fraud inadmissibility after four elements. Passports confiscated/blocked and travellers stranded reported.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiration; fraud finding requires four elements, limited waivers, never automatic. Civil-liberties suit pending, but Supreme Court allowed restrictions in Nov 2025.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy at entry/school/clinic checkpoints can cascade to refusal, investigation, detention and birth-sex placement; state birth-certificate and licence rules reinforce mismatch for residents and parallel traveller screening.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody: trans men reported forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse. National prison model from 2026: hair cutting, hormone removal, psychiatric substitution; reporting of trans prisoners stopped. Student held 24h in men's ward after bathroom arrest.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No documented traveller-specific custody protocol protecting gender identity; some executive orders blocked/enjoined, but passport restriction upheld. Consular or independent monitoring not documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Entry fraud allegation or facility trespass can lead to detention where birth-sex placement and reported abuse increase severity; stopped reporting reduces oversight.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal binary definition bars government single-sex facilities congruent with identity; state law allows restricting trans bathroom use in many state-run facilities. Four states criminalise certain use as trespass; arrest documented 19 Mar 2025, handcuffed, up to 60 days.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Offence requires willful entry plus refusal to depart after request, with exemptions; 29 states and capital district have no mapped ban, but this state's restriction is operative and federal rule applies regardless.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Checkpoint, school, capitol, hospital and transport encounters repeatedly force birth-sex facility use; airport screening can out travellers before facility access.

care_services.exposure: Gender-affirming care for minors banned in state under 2023 veto-proof bill and 27 states nationally; proposed federal bar on public reimbursement under 18. Hospital records subpoenaed nationally. Hormone removal in custody documented.
care_services.protection: Adult care for visitors not documented as banned in dossier; emergency care access not documented. Some federal orders enjoined, status uncertain.
care_services.interaction: Travelling minor may be denied non-emergency continuity care, records may be disclosed, and provider exposure can cause de facto denial even if parent is not defendant.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Executive orders and 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritising groups described as radically pro-transgender; DOJ reward guidance uses radical gender ideology framing. EO directs investigation/prosecution over school social transition. State has no gender-identity discrimination or hate-crime statute.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Strategy states powers not for mere disagreement; national hate-crime prosecution available since 2009; one city municipal protections; 78% in state poll supported anti-discrimination law. Party platform framing was condemned by many delegates and governor.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Threat framing raises likelihood police/school/hospital treat gender diversity as security or safeguarding issue; lack of state cover leaves national floor only.

minors_guardians.exposure: Minor care ban, school and higher-education sports bans for those assigned male at birth, May 2023 pronoun/disclosure law requiring parental disclosure, penalty/emergency-clause student bill, and federal EO investigating schools and teachers facilitating social transition.
minors_guardians.protection: Conversion therapy banned for certain licensed professionals in state; adoption has no express LGBTQ ban, but private agencies may discriminate on religious grounds. No operative shield for visiting families documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: Enrolling a trans minor, seeking care, or using chosen name can trigger disclosure, exclusion, care denial, records scrutiny and enquiry affecting parents/guardians and providers.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No dated incident of violence against a trans person in this state is documented, and no enforcement of the 2023 student-bill penalty is documented; absence is not safety. Police did arrest and handcuff a student for bathroom use. Custody abuse nationally documented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: No documented state hate-crime cover; national prosecution possible. Public opinion supports anti-discrimination, and tribal nations maintain two-spirit traditions, but no traveller policing protocol documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Documented exposure is primarily state action rather than measured street prevalence; unknown community violence cannot be used as mitigation.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Remedies are slow, contested and incomplete: passport suit unresolved, several orders blocked/enjoined but core restrictions allowed to take effect, state lacks gender-identity bias statute, and future state bills pending. Birth-certificate 2023 statute versus 2008 regulation relationship unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Functioning courts, legal aid, ACLU litigation and injunctions on some orders provide partial recourse; 22 states plus capital district ban gender-identity discrimination, though not this state.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Courts working efficiently to enforce hostile passport/facility policy is exposure, while litigation success on other orders only mitigates those issues; timing at travel determines operative rule.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar or slightly higher: both involve birth-sex custody/facility placement and documented abuse risk, but here arrest is first-known rather than routine raids/extortion and courts/legal aid are more functional, placing it above 0.25.

Lower than 0.55-B: secondary screening there usually ends in administrative denial; here criminal trespass, men's-ward detention, custody sexual-abuse reports, minor-care bans and fraud-inadmissibility risk are more severe and compounding.

Far lower than 0.85-A: that anchor has equality law, chosen-name documents, independent oversight and compensation; here operative federal/state rules mandate birth-sex documents and facilities, with thin state recourse and official threat framing.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller encounters one combined system: federal passport, entry, facilities, custody and threat-framing rules interact with state facility, document, sports, disclosure and minor-care bans. The most protective elements—national employment/hate-crime floor, courts, injunctions, city protections and public support—do not pre-empt federal entry or state facility/custody exposure. Universal document and facility checks make outing likely if documents or presentation differ, and documented consequences range from refusal and investigation to arrest, birth-sex detention and severe custody abuse. Minor travellers face additional care, school and disclosure exposures. This severity and compounding place the regime in High Risk, above routine detention anchors but below execution/imprisonment-certain anchors.
